statistics.title: Probability & Statistics
statistics.description: Probability, random variables, estimation, hypothesis testing, ANOVA, and multiple testing.

sections.title: Probability & Events
sections.summary: Events, probability axioms, conditional probability, independence, total probability, and Bayes' theorem.

sections.title: Random Variables & Distributions
sections.summary: Random variables, CDFs, quantiles, discrete and continuous distributions, joint and conditional distributions, and transformations.

sections.title: Expectation, Variance & Dependence
sections.summary: Expectation, variance, covariance, independence, conditional expectation, total variance, and portfolio moments.

sections.title: Point Estimation
sections.summary: Estimator properties, method of moments, maximum likelihood, the law of large numbers, the CLT, and Slutsky's theorem.

sections.title: Hypothesis Testing & Confidence Intervals
sections.summary: Hypotheses, error rates, power, Wald tests, p-values, confidence intervals, and exact versus asymptotic inference.

sections.title: ANOVA
sections.summary: One-way, two-way and three-way ANOVA: factorial designs, main effects, interactions, F tests, degrees of freedom, and replication.

sections.title: Multiple Hypothesis Testing
sections.summary: FWER, FDP, FDR, Bonferroni, Holm, Benjamini-Hochberg, Benjamini-Yekutieli, and FDP-StepM.

econometrics.title: Econometrics
econometrics.description: Cross-sectional regression, pooled samples, panel data, time series, and spatial dependence.

sections.title: OLS Estimation
sections.summary: OLS through derivatives, geometric projection, method of moments and Gaussian maximum likelihood, with partial regression, assumptions and coefficient interpretation.

sections.title: Regression Inference & Diagnostics
sections.summary: Regression tests, VIF, heteroskedasticity diagnostics, robust standard errors, specification, endogeneity and instrumental variables.

sections.title: Pooled cross-sections and parameter stability
sections.summary: Repeated cross-sectional samples, time indicators, changing composition, interaction models, parameter stability, and the distinction from panel pooled OLS.
topics: Repeated samples are not a panel
Allow slopes to change using interactions
Parameter stability is a testable restriction
Pooled OLS is also an estimator for panel data

sections.title: Fixed effects and first differences
sections.summary: Panel structure, unit heterogeneity, within transformation, LSDV, first differences, two-way effects, and clustered inference.
topics: A panel has both unit and time indices
The within transformation removes the unit effect
Worked example: within and between tell different stories
Inference and what fixed effects do not remove

sections.title: Random effects and estimator choice
sections.summary: Random-effects covariance, quasi-demeaning, pooled and within limits, Hausman comparisons, correlated random effects, and practical estimator selection.
topics: Move the unit component into the disturbance
FE, RE, and pooled OLS answer different comparisons
What a Hausman comparison can establish
Correlated random effects makes the restriction visible

sections.title: Dynamic panels and GMM
sections.summary: Lagged outcomes, short-panel bias, difference GMM, system GMM, instrument timing, serial-correlation tests, and instrument proliferation.
topics: Use timing restrictions to build instruments
System GMM adds assumptions, not just equations

sections.title: Stationarity & Unit Roots
sections.summary: Weak and strict stationarity, white noise, ACF, deterministic and stochastic trends, random walks, ADF and KPSS tests, and spurious regression.

sections.title: ARMA & Forecasting
sections.summary: AR, MA, ARMA and ARIMA models, lag polynomials, root conventions, ACF and PACF, information criteria, forecast recursions, and evaluation.

sections.title: VAR, Cointegration & VECM
sections.summary: Multivariate autoregressions, stability, reduced-form shocks, Granger prediction, cointegration, VECM algebra, rank, and adjustment.

sections.title: ARCH & GARCH
sections.summary: Conditional mean and variance, ARCH diagnostics, GARCH persistence and forecasts, GJR-GARCH, EGARCH, heavy-tailed innovations, and tail risk.

sections.title: Spatial Econometrics
sections.summary: Spatial econometrics: spatial weights, SAR feedback and spillovers, estimation, and the SEM, SLX, and SDM models.

learning.title: Statistical Learning
learning.description: Learning from data and evaluating predictions.

sections.title: Model Evaluation
sections.summary: Classification evaluation: decision thresholds, confusion matrices, accuracy, precision, recall, F-scores, and multiclass averaging.

sections.title: Explainable AI (XAI)
sections.summary: Explainable artificial intelligence: local and global explanations, LIME, SHAP, integrated gradients, partial dependence, ICE, ALE, and counterfactuals.

nlp.title: Natural Language Processing
nlp.description: Text representations, topic models, and language models.

sections.title: Bag of Words
sections.summary: Bag of Words (BoW), Term-Document Matrices, TF-IDF, and Vector Space Models in Natural Language Processing.

sections.title: LSA & LDA
sections.summary: Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) via SVD and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) via Bayesian Inference and Dirichlet Priors.

sections.title: Embeddings & Word2Vec
sections.summary: Word Embeddings and Word2Vec: Continuous Bag of Words (CBOW), Skip-Gram, Weight Matrices, and Softmax Prediction.

sections.title: Transformers & BERT
sections.summary: Transformers and BERT Architecture: Self-Attention, Scaled Dot-Product, Positional Encodings, Cross-Attention, and Bidirectional Pre-training.

sections.title: Large Language Models
sections.summary: How large language models generate tokens, how parameter counts compare across 2019–2026 models, how assistants are trained, and what agent harnesses add.

sections.title: Value at Risk
sections.summary: Value-at-Risk (VaR): Formal definition, parametric location-scale models, GARCH & EWMA volatility, Historical Simulation, CAViaR, and out-of-sample backtesting with Kupiec, Christoffersen, and Basel Traffic Light frameworks.

sections.title: Expected Shortfall
sections.summary: Expected Shortfall (ES): Coherent risk measures, Artzner axioms of coherence, conditional tail expectation, and graphical intuition vs. Value-at-Risk (VaR).

sections.title: Sharpe & Sortino Ratios
sections.summary: Risk-adjusted performance metrics: Sharpe Ratio (total volatility) vs. Sortino Ratio (downside risk), mathematical formulations, and comparative intuition.

bayesian.title: Bayesian Statistics
bayesian.description: Prior beliefs, probabilistic models, and posterior inference.
